assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz (2003) model of firm heterogeneity and selection, together with Helpman's work on trade with differentiated products and heterogeneous firms, changed how trade theory and empirics are done. It moved the unit of analysis from industries to firms and gave a tractable account of the welfare gains from trade through reallocation. It is broad, has been widely adopted, and ties tightly to micro data and policy.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the clear originator of the heterogeneous-firm trade framework. Helpman has a long record of foundational work on increasing returns, trade and firm-level margins, and co-authored the key empirical follow-ups. Redding is excluded as a later contributor to quantitative spatial and trade work. Melitz and Helpman are the most defensible pair; some credit could reasonably extend to other contributors, such as Bernard, Eaton and Kortum.
assessment.maturity: The Melitz paper dates from 2003, so more than two decades of confirmation, extension and quantitative use. The field has already recognised the closely related Krugman prize, so the heterogeneous-firm step is a natural successor.
uncertainties: How the committee would weigh credit to other contributors, such as Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, against Helpman and Melitz.
Whether the prize is seen as too close to the earlier trade award.
Whether Helpman's contribution is better described by a different strand of his work, such as the political-economy work in B047.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and the China-shock evidence on local labour-market effects of trade changed the academic and policy debate on inequality, polarisation and adjustment costs. The work combines clear identification with theory and is highly relevant across labour, trade and macro. Its effects on the profession's views about adjustment frictions are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to task-based labour-demand analysis and to the trade-shock papers. Hanson is central to the China-shock and local-adjustment strand. Katz and Dorn are important, but the group is large and the core contributions can be separated. Katz also appears under another candidate, B028. Acemoglu's earlier and parallel work on tasks is outside this entry but complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are from the early 2000s to the 2010s, with a lot of follow-up. Some conclusions about long-run effects are still being refined, as are readings of the China shock and the labour-market response.
uncertainties: Overlap with the task-framework literature associated with Acemoglu and Autor, whose later recognition may complicate credit.
Whether the committee sees the empirical shock papers as a prize-level conceptual advance or as strong applied work.
The subsequent debate over magnitudes and interpretation of the China shock.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes approach to demand estimation with differentiated products, together with Pakes's work on dynamic industry models and estimation, provides core tools now used throughout industrial organisation, antitrust, trade and public finance. The methodological impact is large and has changed practice in merger analysis and market-power measurement.
assessment.attribution: The BLP (1995) trio is the natural core for demand estimation. Pakes also stands behind dynamic oligopoly models and estimation, with Ericson, Olley and others, so his credit extends further. Other listed names, such as Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, contributed in related areas, and the three-name limit forces exclusions.
assessment.maturity: The BLP paper is from 1995 and the method has been used for three decades, with extensive refinement and replication. Confirmation is strong in applied use.
uncertainties: Whether Pakes alone, or Pakes with Berry and Levinsohn, better reflects the credit.
Whether the committee wants to reward structural IO methods after the earlier IO and auction recognition.
Exclusion of Bresnahan and others whose contributions were also substantial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore 'Credit Cycles' showed how collateral constraints create amplification and persistence, and the financial-accelerator line, with Gertler, made credit frictions part of mainstream macro. The work became central after 2008 and remains the base for much macro-finance modelling. It is a major conceptual contribution to macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clearest originators of the collateral-constraint dynamics. Gertler's contribution is the financial accelerator and later work on financial intermediation. Bernanke's financial-accelerator work with Gertler was recognised earlier, in the 2022 prize, which complicates how much more credit Gertler's strand warrants. Gilchrist is a significant empirical contributor but not essential to the core.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from the 1990s. They were strongly validated by the 2007-09 crisis and the subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize recognised related work on banks and financial crises, which may reduce the appetite for another prize in this area.
Whether Gertler should be included, given his recognition via the earlier prize and his appearance in B018.
As a member with macro expertise, I recognise the field's strengths, which may bias my view of its relative importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and the monetary-policy rule framework are the basis of modern central-bank analysis, with a very large influence on both theory and policy. Combining the micro-founded New Keynesian model with an interest-rate rule gave a workable framework for policy evaluation. The importance is beyond doubt; the difficulty is assigning credit.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) and Taylor (1980) are the foundations of staggered pricing and contracts. Taylor's rule is a separate policy contribution. Woodford synthesised the framework and gave the normative analysis. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler made major empirical and quantitative contributions, so the three-name limit leaves out many. Attribution is the weakest part of this candidate.
assessment.maturity: The foundations are 40 to 45 years old and have been tested over decades. The framework was stressed by the 2021-23 inflation episode, and the literature on the Phillips curve and heterogeneity continues to develop.
uncertainties: High attribution diffuseness; any three-person selection omits major contributors, including Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gali and Smets.
Whether the committee views the framework as settled or as still evolving after the inflation episode.
Overlap with earlier prizes for rational-expectations and monetary-policy work, such as those to Lucas, Sargent and Sims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy, the 'Redux' sticky-price model and the exchange-rate disconnect work reshaped international macro. The foundations text, with its dynamic, micro-founded analysis of the current account and exchange rates, provided the working framework. The influence on policy institutions is also large.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair for the Redux model, the foundations text and the exchange-rate puzzles. Other major contributors to the intertemporal approach, such as Sachs, Razin and Svensson, as well as Gourinchas and Rey in later work, are outside this entry. Rogoff also appears in B013 with Reinhart.
assessment.maturity: Core work is from 1995 to 2000. Many of the puzzles remain unresolved, which is both a strength, in sustained interest, and a limit on the finality of the results.
uncertainties: Whether the main findings are a resolved advance or a research agenda with persistent puzzles.
The split of Rogoff's recognition between this and the Reinhart-Rogoff work.
Prior recognition of Mundell, Krugman and others in open-economy work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The top-income and wealth-share series built from tax data changed measurement of inequality and brought it to the centre of public and academic debate. The new data and the evidence on long-run trends strongly influenced public economics, macro and political economy. The data-construction contribution is clearly significant; the theoretical account of r>g is more contested.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income-share series from tax data, with Atkinson as an important earlier and deceased contributor. Zucman is a major contributor on wealth and offshore wealth but more junior. Saez also appears in B039 on optimal taxation.
assessment.maturity: The original top-income work dates from 2003 and later. The wealth-distribution and offshore-wealth results are more recent and still contested on methodology.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth-series construction and the capital-income dynamics.
Whether the committee would treat the work as measurement of a prize-level scientific advance or as influential but contested.
The role of Atkinson, who is deceased, in the historical attribution.
Inequality is adjacent to my own research interests, so I note a possible bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework showed that the dispersion of marginal products across firms can account for large cross-country productivity gaps, and it linked micro data to aggregate development accounting. It is widely used in growth, development and macro. The quantitative importance is a source of debate, since measured misallocation can reflect measurement error and adjustment frictions.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the main originators, with Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) a parallel contribution. A three-name selection would include Restuccia, but the pair Hsieh-Klenow is most associated with the empirical implementation. The three-name limit and near-simultaneous papers create attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from 2008-09, so about 17 years of use. Debate about measurement, and about how much of the gap misallocation explains, is continuing, which lowers its maturity relative to the other entries.
uncertainties: Controversy about how much of the measured dispersion is true misallocation rather than measurement error or adjustment costs.
Whether Restuccia should be included because of the parallel contribution.
Field adjacency: this is in my own broad area of macroeconomics and growth, so I note the possibility of bias.
